html:
Neoplatonism was the last great school of ancient Greek philosophy, a new reading of Plato begun by Plotinus in Rome in the 200s CE. It taught that all things flow from a single source, the One, and that the soul can climb back to it.

Plotinus set out the system in the treatises his student Porphyry collected as the Enneads. From the One, which is beyond thought and beyond being, flows Intellect, which holds the eternal Forms. From Intellect flows Soul, which shapes the visible world. Matter is the dimmest end of the chain. A person can turn inward and, through philosophy and contemplation, rise towards union with the One.

Later teachers added ritual and a crowded ladder of gods. The school's centres were Alexandria, where Hypatia taught, and Athens, where Proclus led the Academy in the 400s. The emperor Justinian's ban on pagan teaching in 529 closed the Athens schools.

Its ideas lived on in the religions that replaced it:

  • In Christianity, through Augustine, who read the Platonists before his conversion, and through mystical writers and Maximus the Confessor.
  • In Islam, through Arabic paraphrases of Plotinus that circulated as a "Theology of Aristotle" and shaped thinkers such as Avicenna, and in the teachings of the Druze.
  • In Renaissance Florence, where Marsilio Ficino translated Plotinus into Latin.
sum: Neoplatonism was the last great school of ancient Greek philosophy, a new reading of Plato begun by Plotinus in Rome in the 200s CE. It taught that all things flow from a single source, the One, and that the soul can climb back to it.
